answer: Grading seats are sold, not handed out per identity, so key count buys nothing. Each epoch 100 panel seats are auctioned with sealed bids signed by falcon, the post-quantum signature scheme, and the auction kernel charges every winner one uniform price, the highest losing bid. An attacker taking k seats must outbid the k honest holders who value seats least, which raises the price on all k, so cost grows as k squared: one seat costs about 1 unit, a 51-seat majority about 2,600. A seat whose holder skips grading turns hollow, its bond burned and the seat resold.
